provisions.text: This Act applies to an operator of a community water system, or a utility distributing electricity serving this state. It provides no assistance and authorizes no amount.

An operator to which this Act applies shall maintain a written plan for continuing service during an interruption, exercise it not less than once in every two years, and file with the department a statement of the date it last did so. A statement filed under this section is not a public record to the extent it describes a vulnerability.
A covered operator shall comply with this Act not later than January 5, 2028.

A utility to which this Act applies shall publish a plan stating the order in which it restores service after an interruption and the basis of that order, and give each affected customer an estimate of when service will be restored and notice when that estimate changes.

provisions.text: This Act applies where a public body of this state offers civilian transition assistance to a person who requests it as a former service member. A request under this Act does not establish veteran status or eligibility for any benefit under other law.

At the person's request, the body shall provide contact information it has checked for a relevant employment, education or benefit inquiry, together with the date checked and any eligibility question the receiving body must decide.

No referral shall be described as acceptance, benefit approval or a determination of service status. Personal information may be transmitted only within the person's consent and otherwise applicable law.
This Act takes effect upon enactment.

provisions.text: This Act amends the eligibility requirements of the Household Utility Assistance Act. It makes no other change to the household utility assistance program, and appropriates nothing.

A household whose income does not exceed 60 per cent of the income limit published by the administering agency for the area in which the household lives qualifies for assistance under the Act named in Section 1. Where the published limit is revised, this section applies to the limit as revised.
This Act applies to determinations made in and after the next program year and has no effect on a determination made after January 5, 2027, when the requirement it amends resumes as it stood before.
The administering agency shall report annually on the number of households qualifying under this Act who did not qualify before it, and on how many of them received assistance.

provisions.text: It is the purpose of this Act to establish what the state's water systems are made of before deciding what replacing them would cost. Nothing in this Act appropriates money or obliges a system to replace a service line.
A community water system serving 3,300 or more connections is subject to this Act. A system below that size may file under this Act voluntarily and is not subject to its deadline.
A covered system shall file the plan required by this Act not later than January 5, 2029. A system that has not filed by that date shall report the reason to the department.

The plan required by this Act shall contain an inventory identifying the material of each service line in the system and the sequence in which the system would replace them. The department shall publish each filed plan.

provisions.text: It is the purpose of this Act to fund replacement of the service lines a filed plan has identified, in an order the statute itself states. Nothing in this Act obliges a system to replace a line the fund does not reach.
A community water system serving 3,300 or more connections that has filed a replacement plan may draw on the fund established by this Act.
There is appropriated to a service line replacement fund a sum not to exceed $29,000,000, available to covered systems that have filed a replacement plan.

The department shall distribute from the fund to the systems with the highest share of service lines identified as requiring replacement, and shall publish the order it applies each year. A system's place in the order is not a guarantee of a distribution.

provisions.text: It is the purpose of this Act to test whether removing the fare barrier increases access to work, care and school for riders who already qualify for state assistance. Nothing in this Act creates an entitlement to service.
A rider is eligible under this Act if the rider is enrolled in a state assistance program at the time of boarding. A participating provider shall not require a separate application.
There is appropriated for the two-year pilot a sum not to exceed $8,000,000, to be distributed among participating providers in proportion to eligible boardings. No provider is named in this section.

provisions.text: A utility serving 25,000 or more customers in this state may apply for an award under this Act. A utility serving fewer may not, and this Act imposes no duty on one.
There is authorized not more than $15,000,000 for awards under this Act, of which no award may exceed half the cost of the work it funds. This section states a ceiling and does not provide the money.
No award may be made under this Act after January 5, 2031.

A utility receiving an award under this Act shall report the completion of each funded work and, for the two years before and the two years after it, the number and total duration of sustained interruptions on the circuits it affected, and the department shall publish what it receives.
